cards.title: OpenAI Launches Visual Ads in Image Generation
cards.body: OpenAI is introducing visual ads that appear after image generation results, initially rolling out in the U.S. only. The move marks the company's expansion into advertising within its creative tools.

cards.title: HackerRank's AI Interviewer Hits 500K Interviews
cards.body: HackerRank's AI interviewer has conducted over 500,000 interviews with major companies like Snowflake and Capgemini. The tool is reshaping how tech hiring could work at scale.

cards.title: Google Freezes Open Source Bug Bounty Program
cards.body: Google paused its open source bug bounty program due to a significant rise in AI-generated submissions. The move highlights how AI spam is overwhelming security research workflows.

cards.title: Trump Administration Launches Super Intelligence Force
cards.body: The Trump administration unveiled a new Super Intelligence Force task force as part of its AI policy response. The initiative addresses ongoing debates around AI safety and development.

cards.title: OpenAI Safety Employee Resigns Over Culture
cards.body: David Robinson, an OpenAI safety employee, resigned claiming the company's culture is broken. His departure adds to growing concerns about safety priorities at leading AI firms.

cards.title: Apple Tightens macOS Full Disk Access Controls
cards.body: Apple is adding new controls to macOS's Full Disk Access permission due to risks from increasingly capable AI agents. The move protects user files, messages, and browsing history from broad AI access.

cards.title: White House Gets Tech CEOs to Sign AI Pledge
cards.body: President Trump convened major tech leaders including Zuckerberg, Bezos, and Musk to sign a morally binding AI safety pledge. The White House is rebranding AI as super intelligence in its policy messaging.

cards.title: Sean Parker Rebuilds Stability AI Around Music
cards.body: Sean Parker is repositioning Stability AI to focus on music generation with music label backing. The move signals a strategic pivot for the company.

cards.title: Meta Open-Sources Muse for Consumer Devices
cards.body: Meta is releasing Muse code for free to encourage adoption across consumer electronics like TVs and appliances. The strategy aims to embed Meta's AI capabilities broadly across devices.

cards.title: Amazon Defends Data Centers, Drops NDAs
cards.body: AWS CEO pushed back against data center skepticism by announcing the company no longer uses NDAs. The transparency move comes amid widespread concerns about data center practices.

cards.title: Hot Girl Hotline Offers AI Dating Advice
cards.body: Two sisters founded Hot Girl Hotline, an AI service providing personalized dating and relationship advice to young women. The platform emphasizes safety and avoids fostering emotional dependency.

cards.title: Researchers Track Chinese AI Agent Swarm
cards.body: Independent researchers discovered an AI agent swarm running on Tencent's infrastructure targeting Alibaba's Amap service. The discovery raises questions about competitive AI operations in China.

cards.title: Safeworld Builds Digital Humans for Robot Safety
cards.body: Safeworld is developing digital humans to ensure robots won't harm real people. The company addresses growing concerns about AI agent and robotics safety.

cards.title: AI Agents Now Available in Text Messages
cards.body: Multiple AI agents can now operate within text messaging platforms for various use cases. Options range from general assistants to specialized agents for families, travel, and work.

cards.title: Consumer Skepticism on Super Intelligence Remains High
cards.body: Only 2% of consumers are buying into the super intelligence messaging promoted by the administration and tech companies. Public sentiment lags far behind industry and government enthusiasm for the technology.

cards.title: Connecting AI agents to enterprise knowledge
cards.body: Enterprise AI agents often lack organizational context despite processing vast amounts of data. Knowledge—understanding what data means within specific business contexts—is critical for AI systems to function effectively.

cards.title: Bringing predictive analytics to agentic AI era
cards.body: Predictive models now reliably outperform statistical forecasts, but the real challenge is enabling them to act autonomously while staying aligned with business goals. The frontier has shifted from prediction accuracy to maintaining business intent in AI actions.

cards.title: People hate AI, yet can't stop using it
cards.body: Despite public skepticism toward AI, adoption continues to surge across sectors. This paradox reflects tension between distrust of AI capabilities and the genuine utility these systems provide.

cards.title: When AI meets biology, infrastructure, and science
cards.body: Google Research VP explores AI's expanding impact beyond traditional applications into biology, infrastructure, and manufacturing. The greatest breakthroughs may emerge where AI intersects with multiple disciplines.

cards.title: Redefining enterprise intelligence with autonomous AI
cards.body: Enterprise AI is now operationally deployed at scale with capabilities advancing faster than organizations can adopt them. Global AI investment is projected to reach $2.5 trillion in 2026, a 44% increase year-over-year.

cards.title: Don't be fooled—LLMs don't actually reason
cards.body: Large language models generate plausible text patterns but lack true reasoning capabilities. Understanding this limitation is crucial for realistic expectations about AI system abilities.

cards.title: AI tool reconstructs images from brain scans
cards.body: A new AI system can predict what you're viewing based solely on brain scan analysis. This breakthrough demonstrates novel applications of AI in neuroscience and cognitive research.

cards.title: Apple restricts full-disk access to curb AI agents
cards.body: Apple modified permissions to prevent unauthorized access by AI agents on its platform. The move reflects growing security concerns as autonomous AI systems become more prevalent.

cards.title: AI glasses face first major government crackdown
cards.body: Regulatory bodies are beginning to restrict AI-powered glasses technology, marking a significant policy shift. Privacy and surveillance concerns are driving the enforcement action.
